mainTopic: The closing aggadot of מסכת ברכות: רבי אבין הלוי's teachings, the praise of תלמידי חכמים, and the peace they bring
overview: This amud closes מסכת ברכות. It first finishes a proof from פסוקים that עובד אדום was blessed with sixty-two descendants for honoring the ארון. Then רבי אבין הלוי teaches that whoever forces an opportunity loses it, while whoever steps back from it is rewarded. The proof is the story of רב יוסף (סיני) and רבה (עוקר הרים): רב יוסף was chosen but stepped aside, and he still led later, after רבה's twenty-two years. More teachings of רבי אבין הלוי follow: why a verse says 'אלהי יעקב', the holiness of a meal with a תלמיד חכם, and the right way to say goodbye, 'לך לשלום' to the living and 'לך בשלום' to the dead. Next come teachings praising תלמידי חכמים: going from בית הכנסת to בית המדרש earns פני שכינה, and scholars keep growing even in עולם הבא. The מסכת ends with the teaching that תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world, and with verses about שלום.

steps.title: Verses showing the blessing of עובד אדום's sixty-two descendants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer from דברי הימים that עובד אדום was blessed with eight sons, and that the family grew to sixty-two.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is stated: "פעלתי the eighth," and it is written: "For God blessed him." And: "All these were of the sons of עובד אדום, they and their sons and their brethren, able men in strength for the service: sixty-two of עובד אדום."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it started on the previous amud. It quotes פסוקים showing that the many children of עובד אדום were a ברכה for honoring the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק lists eight sons and then says 'for God blessed him,' so the eight sons themselves are the blessing. The second פסוק gives a total of sixty-two. The earlier text explained the math: nine women each gave birth to six, which makes fifty-four, plus the original eight, which makes sixty-two.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is stated (introduces a proof from a פסוק)
The man who hosted the ארון in his home for three months

steps.whatToRemember: Honoring the ארון brought עובד אדום a huge blessing of children: sixty-two descendants.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "Peulletai the eighth,"
phrases.notes: The eighth son listed for עובד אדום.

phrases.english: and it is written: "For God blessed him."
phrases.notes: The פסוק is telling us all those sons came from God's blessing.

phrases.english: "All these were of the sons of Oved-edom,
they and their sons and their brethren,
able men in strength for the service:
sixty-two of Oved-edom."
phrases.notes: Fifty-four born from the nine women, plus the original eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and closes the proof earlier (63b) about the blessing of עובד אדום.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that עובד אדום's family was blessed with many births

steps.title: רבי אבין הלוי: forcing the moment versus yielding to it
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין הלוי teaches that someone who forces an opportunity loses it, and someone who steps back from an opportunity is eventually rewarded by it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין הלוי said: Whoever pushes the moment, the moment pushes him away. And whoever steps aside before the moment, the moment steps aside for him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רבי אבין הלוי states a life principle about grabbing opportunities versus giving them up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pushing for an opportunity that is not yet meant for you backfires, and it slips away. Yielding works the other way: if you step back, the opportunity eventually comes to you on its own. The גמרא will prove this next with a story.

keyTerms.meaning: One who yields or steps aside

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'שעה דוחקתו' as 'the moment presses him on.' It means the opportunity pushes him away, so he loses it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin HaLevi said:
Whoever pushes the moment,
phrases.notes: Tries to grab an opportunity before its time.

phrases.english: the moment pushes him away.
And whoever steps aside before the moment,
the moment steps aside for him.
phrases.notes: The opportunity eventually waits for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין הַלֵּוִי: כׇּל הַדּוֹחֵק אֶת הַשָּׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, independent aggadic teaching, unrelated to the topic of עובד אדום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forcing an opportunity makes you lose it, and yielding an opportunity makes it come to you.

steps.title: Background: רבה and רב יוסף as candidates for leadership
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces its proof: רב יוסף was called סיני, רבה was called עוקר הרים, and the time came to choose a leader.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is learned from רבה and רב יוסף. רב יוסף was "סיני" and רבה was "עוקר הרים" (one who uproots mountains), and the moment came when they were needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a story that will prove רבי אבין הלוי's teaching. It introduces the two great candidates for ראש ישיבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סיני describes someone with vast, organized knowledge of the sources, like the Torah as given at סיני. עוקר הרים describes someone with brilliant analytical sharpness. 'The moment came' means the yeshiva needed a new head.

keyTerms.meaning: Nickname for a scholar with encyclopedic knowledge of the sources
Uprooter of mountains, a scholar with brilliant analytical sharpness
The moment arrived when they were needed (to appoint a leader)

phrases.english: From Rabba and Rav Yosef.
phrases.notes: Here comes the story that proves it.

phrases.english: For Rav Yosef was "Sinai"
phrases.notes: He knew an enormous amount of Torah.

phrases.english: and Rabba was "one who uproots mountains,"
phrases.notes: He was incredibly sharp at working through a sugya.

phrases.english: the moment came when they were needed.
phrases.notes: One had to be chosen as head of the yeshiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the story that proves רבי אבין הלוי's principle.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבין הלוי's principle about yielding to the moment
steps.raayaSupportSource: The historical episode of רבה and רב יוסף

steps.title: The question sent to ארץ ישראל: who comes first?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of בבל asked the חכמי ארץ ישראל whether the master of knowledge or the master of sharpness should be chosen first.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent a question there: סיני and עוקר הרים, which of them comes first?
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of בבל could not decide, so they sent the question to ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real clarifying question about leadership priorities: is broad knowledge or sharp reasoning more important in a ראש ישיבה?

phrases.english: They sent there:
phrases.notes: To the חכמי ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: סִינַי וְעוֹקֵר הָרִים, אֵיזֶה מֵהֶם קוֹדֵם?
phrases.english: Sinai and one who uproots mountains, which of them takes precedence?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story by presenting the dilemma.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether erudition (סיני) or analytical sharpness (עוקר הרים) takes precedence for leadership.

steps.title: The answer: סיני comes first
steps.stepSummary: ארץ ישראל answered that סיני takes precedence, because everyone depends on the one who holds the sources.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent back to them: סיני comes first, because everyone needs the owner of the wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמי ארץ ישראל answer the question in favor of רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The owner of the wheat' is a parable. Sharp reasoning is like grinding, but without wheat there is nothing to grind. Whoever holds the raw material, meaning the sources, is the one everyone needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Owner of the wheat, a parable for the master of the sources

phrases.english: They sent to them: Sinai takes precedence,
for everyone needs the owner of the wheat.
phrases.notes: Someone who knows the sources inside out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סיני takes precedence because all depend on the master of the sources.
steps.whyThisMatters: This became a famous principle about valuing broad knowledge of sources as the foundation of Torah learning.

steps.title: רב יוסף declines the position
steps.stepSummary: Even though he was chosen, רב יוסף refused the post, because astrologers had told him he would rule for only two years.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, רב יוסף did not accept it, because the כלדאי astrologers had told him: You will rule for two years.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the key moment of the proof. רב יוסף 'yields to the moment' and gives up the position he had won.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף feared that once he took leadership, he would die after two years. So he stepped aside and let רבה lead. This is the 'נדחה מפני השעה' of רבי אבין הלוי's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Did not accept it upon himself

phrases.english: Even so,
Rav Yosef did not accept it upon himself,
because the Chaldeans had told him:
You will rule for two years.
phrases.notes: He understood this to mean he would die after two years of leadership.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן לֹא קִבֵּל עָלָיו רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A twist: despite winning, רב יוסף yields the position.
steps.raayaObject: The 'yielding to the moment' half of רבי אבין הלוי's principle

steps.title: The outcome: both men led in turn
steps.stepSummary: רבה led for twenty-two years, and after him רב יוסף led for two and a half years. The moment waited for the one who yielded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה ruled for twenty-two years. רב יוסף ruled for two and a half years.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by showing how things turned out, which completes the proof of רבי אבין הלוי's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because רב יוסף stepped aside, the leadership waited for him. He still got his turn after רבה's twenty-two years. His destined term only began then, so his yielding did not cost him the position.

keyTerms.meaning: Ruled, here meaning served as ראש ישיבה

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף yielded the moment, and the moment yielded to him: he still became ראש ישיבה, just later. This proves רבי אבין הלוי's teaching.

phrases.english: Rabba ruled for twenty-two years,

phrases.aramaic: מְלַךְ רַב יוֹסֵף תַּרְתֵּין שְׁנִין וּפַלְגָא.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef ruled for two and a half years.
phrases.notes: After רבה's death, fulfilling what was destined for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of רב יוסף's yielding, which closes the proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One who yields to the moment is not pushed aside. רב יוסף still received leadership in its proper time.

steps.title: רב יוסף did not even summon a bloodletter
steps.stepSummary: During all of רבה's years as leader, רב יוסף did not use even the smallest bit of authority. He would not even call a bloodletter to his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the years that רבה ruled, רב יוסף did not even call a bloodletter to his home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one final detail to the רב יוסף story. It shows how completely he stepped aside while רבה was in charge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling a craftsman to come to you is a small act of importance. רב יוסף avoided even that and went to the bloodletter himself. This proves that his yielding was total and sincere, which is why the moment later 'waited' for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A bloodletter (a craftsman who let blood for health)
Ruled, served as head of the yeshiva

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף gave up even the tiniest signs of authority. That full humility is the lesson of the whole story: whoever steps aside for the moment, the moment steps aside for him.

phrases.english: All those years that Rabba ruled,
he (Rav Yosef) did not even call a bloodletter to his home.
phrases.notes: He went to the bloodletter instead, so he would not act like someone important.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a closing detail that shows how fully רב יוסף yielded during רבה's twenty-two years.
steps.raayaObject: That רב יוסף truly and completely stepped aside
steps.raayaSupportSource: His behavior: he never summoned even a bloodletter to his house

steps.title: Why does the verse say only 'אלהי יעקב'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין הלוי asks why the verse in תהלים mentions only אלהי יעקב and leaves out אברהם and יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין הלוי also said: What does the verse mean, 'ה׳ will answer you on the day of trouble; the name of the God of יעקב will raise you up'? Why the God of יעקב and not the God of אברהם and יצחק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבי אבין הלוי. It opens with a question about the wording of a verse, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually all three אבות are mentioned together. Here the verse names only יעקב, and רבי אבין הלוי wants to know why. This is a question about the verse's precise wording.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?
Will raise you up, protect you

steps.confusionAlert: 'וְאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין הַלֵּוִי' (and רבי אבין הלוי said) does not mean the רב יוסף story is still going on. The גמרא is simply adding more teachings from the same sage, whose earlier teaching that story illustrated.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Avin HaLevi said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
'The Lord will answer you on the day of trouble;
the name of the God of Jacob will raise you up' (Psalms 20:2)?

phrases.aramaic: אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב וְלֹא אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק?
phrases.english: The God of Jacob, and not the God of Abraham and Isaac?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching from רבי אבין הלוי, separate from the רב יוסף story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the verse names only יעקב and not all three אבות

steps.title: The owner of the beam carries the thick end
steps.stepSummary: The answer is a general principle: the one who owns the beam carries its heavy, thick end. יעקב, who struggled most in raising his children, is the one most fitting to stand by them in their trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here we learn that the owner of the beam should go in under the thick part of the beam.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין הלוי answers his question with a comparison to someone carrying a heavy beam.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever has the most at stake should carry the heaviest part. יעקב suffered greatly raising the family that became the Jewish people, so his merit and connection to them in their distress is the strongest. That is why the verse calls on his name in particular.

keyTerms.meaning: Its thickness, the thick, heavy end

steps.whyThisMatters: This became a well-known saying: whoever is most responsible for something must take on its heaviest part.

phrases.english: From here we learn that the owner of the beam
should go in under the thick part of the beam.
phrases.notes: רש"י: יעקב had the most trouble raising his children, so he is the one to pray for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 about why only יעקב is named.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The one with the most at stake carries the heaviest load. יעקב, who suffered most in raising the nation, is the one associated with helping them in their distress.

steps.title: Eating with a תלמיד חכם is like enjoying the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין הלוי teaches that enjoying a meal where a תלמיד חכם is present is like enjoying the splendor of the שכינה. He brings a verse about the elders eating with יתרו 'before God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין הלוי also said: Whoever enjoys a meal at which a תלמיד חכם is present is as if he enjoyed the splendor of the שכינה, as it says: 'And אהרן came, and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with משה's father-in-law before God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third teaching of רבי אבין הלוי. It states his rule and quotes the verse he will use to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is surprising: an ordinary meal becomes something holy when a Torah scholar is there. The verse is quoted here, but the proof itself depends on the question asked in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The radiant splendor of the Divine Presence

phrases.english: And Rabbi Avin HaLevi said:
Whoever enjoys a meal
at which a Torah scholar is present,
it is as if he enjoyed the splendor of the Divine Presence,
as it is stated: 'And Aaron came,
and all the elders of Israel, to eat bread
with Moses' father-in-law before God' (Exodus 18:12).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין הַלֵּוִי: כׇּל הַנֶּהֱנֶה מִסְּעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate teaching from the same sage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Enjoying a meal where a תלמיד חכם is present is like enjoying the splendor of the שכינה.

steps.title: Did they really eat before God?
steps.stepSummary: The verse cannot be taken literally. The elders were not eating in front of God; they were eating in front of משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did they really eat before God? Didn't they eat before משה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem with reading the verse literally. This problem sets up the lesson in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scene was a meal held in משה's presence, so the words 'before God' look strange. This difficulty is what makes the proof work: the verse must be teaching something by calling that meal 'before God.'

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so? (introduces a doubtful question)

phrases.english: Did they actually eat before God?
But surely they ate before Moses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the literal meaning of the verse quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading of 'לִפְנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים' in the verse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The meal actually took place in front of משה, not God, so the literal words seem inaccurate.

steps.title: The verse teaches the value of a scholar's presence
steps.stepSummary: The verse calls the meal 'before God' to teach that eating with a תלמיד חכם is like enjoying the splendor of the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse comes to tell you that whoever enjoys a meal at which a תלמיד חכם is present is as if he enjoyed the splendor of the שכינה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the difficulty and finishes the proof of רבי אבין הלוי's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since they really ate before משה, calling it 'before God' tells us that sitting with a Torah scholar counts as being before the שכינה. The odd wording of the verse becomes the source of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it comes to tell you

steps.whatToRemember: A meal with a Torah scholar is spiritually elevated. The verse calls eating before משה 'eating before God.'

phrases.english: Rather, it is to tell you:
whoever enjoys a meal
at which a Torah scholar is present
is as if he enjoyed the splendor of the Divine Presence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty of step 12 and confirms the rule of step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Calling a meal before משה 'before God' teaches that eating with a תלמיד חכם is like enjoying the splendor of the שכינה.

steps.title: How to say goodbye to a friend
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין הלוי rules that when you part from a friend, you should say 'לך לשלום' and not 'לך בשלום'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבין הלוי said: Someone parting from his friend should not tell him 'Go in peace.' He should say 'Go to peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another saying of רבי אבין הלוי. This one is a practical rule about the right words to use when saying goodbye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two phrases differ by one letter: ב (in) versus ל (to). 'לך לשלום' wishes the person a journey that keeps moving toward peace and success. The proof for this rule comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes leave / parts from someone
'Go to peace': the correct blessing for a living person
'Go in peace': the wording to avoid with a living person

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the single letter! ל = 'to' and ב = 'in'. The whole rule depends on that one letter, and the next steps flip it for the dead.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Avin HaLevi said:
One who takes leave of his friend
should not say to him 'Go in peace,'
but rather 'Go to peace,'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, independent saying by the same speaker as Steps 9–13 (רבי אבין הלוי).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When parting from a living person, say 'לך לשלום', not 'לך בשלום'.

steps.title: Proof from יתרו and from דוד
steps.stepSummary: יתרו told משה 'לך לשלום' and משה succeeded. דוד told אבשלום 'לך בשלום' and אבשלום ended up hanged.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we see that יתרו said to משה 'Go to peace,' and משה went up and succeeded. דוד said to אבשלום 'Go in peace,' and אבשלום went and was hanged.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין הלוי backs up his rule with two stories from תנ"ך that show what happens with each wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are set side by side as opposites. 'לשלום' was followed by success: משה went on to redeem the Jewish people. 'בשלום' was followed by disaster: אבשלום rebelled and died caught by his hair in a tree. The different outcomes show which wording is the good one.

keyTerms.meaning: For behold / as we see: introduces a proof
דוד's son, who rebelled against him

phrases.english: for Jethro, who said to Moses
'Go to peace': [Moses] went up and succeeded.
David, who said to Absalom
'Go in peace': [Absalom] went and was hanged.
phrases.notes: See שמות ד:יח and שמואל ב טו:ט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for the rule stated in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a living person should be told 'לך לשלום'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The opposite outcomes of משה (blessed with 'לשלום') and אבשלום (blessed with 'בשלום').

steps.title: How to say goodbye to the dead
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין הלוי rules the reverse for the dead: say 'לך בשלום', based on the verse said to אברהם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבין הלוי said: Someone parting from a dead person should not say 'Go to peace.' He should say 'Go in peace,' as the verse says: 'And you shall come to your fathers in peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין הלוי gives a second rule that flips the first: for someone who has died, the right wording is 'לך בשלום'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a verse where הקב"ה tells אברהם he will die peacefully, and it uses 'בשלום'. A living person is still on a journey, so we wish him 'toward' peace. A person who has passed away has reached his rest, so we say 'in' peace.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said: introduces a verse

steps.whatToRemember: Living person: לך לשלום. Dead person: לך בשלום.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Avin HaLevi said:
One who takes leave of a dead person
should not say to him 'Go to peace,'
but rather 'Go in peace,'
as it is said: 'And you shall come to your fathers in peace.'
phrases.notes: בראשית טו:טו, said to אברהם about his death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A companion rule to Step 14 that reverses the wording for the dead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When parting from the dead, say 'לך בשלום', learned from the verse said to אברהם.

steps.title: From בית הכנסת straight to בית המדרש
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי בר חייא teaches that one who goes from בית הכנסת directly to בית המדרש to learn merits greeting the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חייא said: One who leaves the בית הכנסת, enters the בית המדרש and learns Torah merits to greet the שכינה, as it says: 'They go from strength to strength; they appear before God in ציון.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher, רבי לוי בר חייא, praises the person who goes straight from davening to learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the verse as a road map. 'From strength to strength' means going from one holy place (בית הכנסת) to the next (בית המדרש). The verse ends with 'appearing before God in Zion', which he takes as the reward: meriting פני שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: Study hall: the place of Torah learning

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi bar Ḥiyya said:
One who leaves the synagogue
and enters the study hall and engages in Torah
merits and receives the Divine Presence,
as it is said: 'They go from strength to strength,
[each] appears before God in Zion.'
phrases.notes: תהלים פד:ח

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, unrelated teaching by a different sage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going directly from prayer to Torah study earns one the privilege of greeting the שכינה.

steps.title: Torah scholars never stop growing
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches, using the same verse, that תלמידי חכמים have no rest in this world or in the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: תלמידי חכמים have no rest, not in עולם הזה and not in עולם הבא, as it says: 'They go from strength to strength; they appear before God in ציון.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב reads the very same verse in a new way, as a description of the endless climb of תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, 'from strength to strength' means always moving up, one level after the next. Even 'appearing before God in ציון', which is עולם הבא, is not a stop; the climbing continues there too. 'No rest' here is praise: they keep growing forever.
steps.confusionAlert: 'No rest' is not a punishment or a complaint. It means the scholar never stops rising from level to level. Also note that this is the same verse as Step 17, used to teach a different idea.
steps.whatToRemember: The same verse teaches two things: going from davening to learning brings פני שכינה, and true Torah scholars keep growing forever, even in עולם הבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב's reading turns 'no rest' into high praise. A תלמיד חכם never reaches a final resting level; his growth continues even in עולם הבא.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
Torah scholars have no rest

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה וְלֹא בָּעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: neither in this world nor in the World to Come,
as it is said: 'They go from strength to strength,
[each] appears before God in Zion.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same verse as Step 17 to teach a second lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah scholars are always rising and have no resting point, in this world or the next.

steps.title: Torah scholars increase peace in the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי חנינא, teaches that תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world, and brings a verse from ישעיהו as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: Torah scholars bring more peace into the world, as the verse says: 'And all your children are taught by ה׳, and great is the peace of your children.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching: תלמידי חכמים make the world more peaceful. It supports this with a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new statement, by רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא, again about תלמידי חכמים: they bring peace into the world. The verse links being 'taught by ה׳' with 'great peace.' The next step shows how a different reading of one word makes this a direct proof.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a verse)

steps.whyThisMatters: This whole passage is said in many communities after אין כאלקינו, just before קדיש דרבנן, so many learners already know these words from davening.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Chanina said:
Torah scholars increase peace in the world,
as it is said: 'And all your children are taught by ה׳,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 54:13

phrases.english: and great is the peace of your children.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of תלמידי חכמים from step 18, moving from their lack of rest to the peace they bring.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world.

steps.title: Reading 'your children' as 'your builders'
steps.stepSummary: The verse is re-read: instead of בָּנָיִךְ (your children), read בּוֹנָיִךְ (your builders). Torah scholars are the builders of peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not read the word as 'your children.' Read it as 'your builders.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the verse proves the point by reading one word differently. 'Your children' becomes 'your builders.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the verse says that children who learn from ה׳ have peace. With the אל תקרי reading, it says that the 'builders,' the Torah scholars, are the ones who create great peace. This turns the verse into direct support for רבי חנינא's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: do not read (it this way), but rather another way; a drasha technique

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not mean we change the written text of the פסוק. It adds an extra layer of meaning based on a different way of pronouncing the same letters.

phrases.english: Do not read 'your children,'
but rather 'your builders.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the verse from step 19 supports the claim about תלמידי חכמים.
steps.raayaObject: That תלמידי חכמים are the builders of peace.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 54:13, read as בּוֹנָיִךְ instead of בָּנָיִךְ.

steps.title: A chain of verses about peace
steps.stepSummary: Several verses from תהלים are brought, all connecting Torah and its lovers with peace. The chain ends with 'ה׳ will bless His people with peace.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Those who love Your Torah have great peace, and nothing makes them stumble.' 'May there be peace in your walls, calm in your palaces.' 'For the sake of my brothers and friends, I will say: peace be with you. For the sake of the House of ה׳ our God, I will seek good for you.' 'ה׳ will give strength to His people; ה׳ will bless His people with peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a string of verses that all praise peace and connect it to Torah. This is the closing of the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first verse ties peace directly to those who love Torah. The middle verses describe peace inside ירושלים and the בית המקדש. The last verse uses 'strength' (עֹז), which חז״ל often read as Torah, so Torah brings ה׳'s blessing of peace.

keyTerms.meaning: strength (often read by חז״ל as Torah)

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת ברכות ends with the word שלום. Torah learning, done by תלמידי חכמים, is what builds real peace in the world.

phrases.english: 'Great peace to those who love Your Torah,
phrases.notes: תהלים 119:165

phrases.english: and there is no stumbling block for them.'
'May there be peace within your walls,
phrases.notes: תהלים 122:7

phrases.english: tranquility within your palaces.'
'For the sake of my brothers and friends,
phrases.notes: תהלים 122:8–9

phrases.english: I will now say: peace be within you.
For the sake of the House of ה׳ our God,
I will seek good for you.'
'ה׳ will give strength to His people;
phrases.notes: תהלים 29:11

phrases.english: ה׳ will bless His people with peace.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more verses supporting the link between Torah scholars and peace.
steps.raayaObject: That Torah and those who love it bring peace.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הרואה and מסכת ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק הרואה and for all of מסכת ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הרואה, and מסכת ברכות is completed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the argument. It is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the chapter and of the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן עלך expresses our hope to come back and learn this chapter again. סליקא לה tells us the whole מסכת ברכות is now finished.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of the ninth and final chapter of ברכות

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת ברכות is complete. It opened with קריאת שמע and closes with a blessing of שלום.

phrases.english: We will return to you, [chapter] HaRo'eh,
and Tractate Berakhot is completed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הדרן עלך הרואה וסליקא לה מסכת ברכות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter and the מסכת after the final teaching on peace.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק הרואה and of מסכת ברכות.
